 Appearance:
 NISHIT A BHALODI(9597) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MS KIRTI S PATHAK(9966) for the Respondent(s) No. 2  RULE NOT RECD BACK for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ================================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 11/03/2025  ORAL ORDER 1.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 1298 days caused in filing the First Appeal.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.Nishit Bhalodi for the applicant and learned advocate Ms Kirti S.
Pathak for the respondent No.2.
3.
Learned advocate for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has good case on merits as well as on law.
It is further submitted that applicant had to collect necessary NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/492/2025 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined papers and arrange Court fees and other expenses.
It is further submitted that delay may be condoned as there is no intentional delay on the part of the applicants.
3.1 It is further submitted that the present applicant is unaware of the provisions of law, which could permit him to file appeal, which is a statutory right.

Under the instructions, he has further submitted that in view of the settled principles of law in the deceision of Vikrambhai Malabhai Pagi vs Jayantibhai Tejabhai Makwana on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40114190/
1

entities.text: Vikrambhai Malabhai Pagi vs Jayantibhai Tejabhai Makwana on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hon'ble Apex Court in case of K. Subbarayadu and others Vs.

The Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) reported in 2017(12) SCC 840 and would submit that considering the law laid down in aforementioned case, the applicant is not claiming his right for the interest upon the enhanced compensation, if any, for the delay period, if appellant succeeds in First Appeal.

4. Per contra, learned advocate for the respondent has objected and submitted that the reasons assigned in the NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/492/2025 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined application does not inspire any confidence to condone the delay and therefore, application may be dismissed by this Court.
5.

Considering the submissions canvassed by the learned advocates for the parties and contentions raised in the application, it is needless to observe that in catena of decisions, the view taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court is, while deciding an application for condonation of delay, the liberal and justice orientated approach needs to be adopted so that the substantive rights of the parties are not defeated only on the ground of delay.
To meet with the equity, delay can be condoned.
There is no intentional delay on the part of the applicant.
The delay has sufficiently been explained.
Hence, the delay is condoned subject to condition that the claimant/s shall not claim interest upon enhanced compensation, if any, for the period of delay, if succeeds in the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/492/2025 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined 6.
With these observations and directions, the present Civil Application stands allowed.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
(D. M. DESAI,J) RINKU MALI Vikrambhai Malabhai Pagi vs Jayantibhai Tejabhai Makwana on 11 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40114190/
